field.currentPrice.help: What you charge for it today, to compare against the recommendation. Leave it at zero to skip the comparison.
field.grams.help: The weight of the part itself, supports included. The purge below is counted on top.
field.hours.help.mesh: Estimated from the volume and the speed in Setup. Type your slicer's figure in to be exact.
field.hours.help.sliced: What the slicer worked out. Type over it to try another figure.
field.parts.help: How many copies were on the plate. The time and the filament are divided by this to price one part.
field.plate.help: Which sliced plate to price. All of them adds the plates up.
field.postMinutes.help: Minutes spent taking off supports, sanding, assembling and packing it. The part of the job almost everyone gives away.
field.purgeGrams.help: Filament that goes in the bin: purge towers and colour changes. On a multicolour print it can outweigh the part.
field.quantity.help: How many of it are being sold. It changes the order total, not what one costs.
field.scale.help: Printing it larger or smaller. Everything is measured again at this size.

setup.f.currency.help: The sign to put in front of the money. Nothing is converted: type the figures in whatever you sell in.
setup.f.density.help: What a cubic centimetre of it weighs. PLA is 1.24, PETG 1.27, ABS 1.04 — the spool's label says.
setup.f.efficiency.help: The share of that speed actually reached: the printer is forever accelerating into a corner, so it never holds the full figure. This is the dial to turn if the estimated time comes out wrong — raise it if the estimate is long, lower it if it's short.
setup.f.failRate.help: Out of a hundred prints, how many go in the bin. Leaving it at zero claims you never fail, which is exactly the assumption that quietly loses money.
setup.f.fee.help: What the platform keeps, commission and card charges together. It's taken off the selling price, as the platform takes it. Selling in person, it's zero.
setup.f.hourlyRate.help: What you want to be paid an hour. If you're unsure, start with what your day job pays you.
setup.f.kwhPrice.help: What a kilowatt-hour costs you. It's on your bill.
setup.f.lifespan.help: How many printing hours you expect out of it before retiring it. Its cost is spread over those hours, the way a shop writes a machine off.
setup.f.lineWidth.help: The width of one extruded line, usually a little over the nozzle's size.
setup.f.margin.help: What you want on top of the cost. Below 20% there's nothing left to reinvest or to absorb a surprise.
setup.f.overhang.help: A face shallower than this needs holding up. Slicers call it the support threshold; 45° is the usual.
setup.f.packaging.help: Bag, box, label and filler for one.
setup.f.perLayer.help: Seconds a layer that aren't extruding: travel, the Z move, the seam, retractions.
setup.f.postMinutes.help: The default minutes of your own work on a part. Each part can be given its own.
setup.f.price.help: What the machine cost, upgrades and spare parts included.
setup.f.solidLayers.help: Solid layers on the top and on the bottom, each.
setup.f.speed.help: The printing speed your profile asks for.
setup.f.spoolPrice.help: What you paid for the whole spool, postage included.
setup.f.spoolWeight.help: Grams of filament on it, not counting the reel. 1 kg is standard; 750 g and 250 g spools exist.
setup.f.supports.help: Whether to add what supports would weigh to the estimate.
setup.f.walls.help: How many lines thick the outside is.
setup.f.watts.help: Average watts while printing. PLA on an enclosed printer sits around 100–120 W; a hot bed pushes it higher.
setup.kept: Kept on this Thingport, for you
setup.printer.g3.hint: What the estimate from a shape is built on. A sliced file's own figures are used instead whenever there are any.
